question.problem: Evaluate the integral ${\int }_{C}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}s$, where the curve $C$ is given in polar form by $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{6}.$
question.worked_solution:
In polar coordinates, the formula for the line integral is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

 

The connection between polar and Cartesian coordinates gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

So, along our curve, we have $x=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta $, where $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{6}.$

Now, if $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )^{2} \\  & =27{sin}^{5}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  & =\sqrt{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}27{sin}^{5}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 3\cdot \text{d}\theta  \\  & =81{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}{sin}^{5}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}81{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}{sin}^{5}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  & =81{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{u}^{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =81\cdot \frac{1}{6}{u}^{6}\,{|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{27}{2}((\frac{1}{2})^{6}-{0}^{6}) \\  & =\frac{27}{128}\end{aligned}
$$
